title: Custom initial UI settings
description:
Would it be possible for `diffviewer::visual_diff()` to support custom initial values for UI settings such as magnification (1:4 vs 1:2 vs 1:1 vs 2:1), type of view ("Difference" vs "Toggle" vs "Slider"), and which image is selected ("Old" vs "New")?

I am building a Shiny app with a user-side `diffviewer` widget, and in my use case, the current default "Difference" view is not useful because the images are usually different. I'd like to directly supply 1:1 magnification and the "Slider" view as arguments in the call to `diffviewer::visual_diff()`.

title: Add support for comparing complex object structures?
description: (supercedes #27) It would help my workflows for `expect_snapshot_file()` to provide human-readable snapshot reviews for rds files. For example, consider this test: ```r compare_file_object <- function(old, new) { # Load the RDS files old_obj <- readRDS(old) new_obj <- readRDS(new) identical(old_obj, new_obj, ignore.environment = TRUE) } test_that("expect_snapshot_file works with RDS format", { test_obj <- list(x = 1:4, y = c("a", "b", "c")) # test_obj <- list(x = 1:5, y = c("a", "b", "c")) path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") saveRDS(test_obj, path) testthat::expect_snapshot_file( path = path, name = paste0("test_obj.rds"), compare = compare_file_object ) }) ``` 1. run the test to establish the snapshot. 2. uncomment the line `# test_obj <- list(x = 1:5, y = c("a", "b", "c"))` 3. run the test again; should produce a "Snapshot of `path` has changed." message 4. run `testthat::snapshot_review()` current output (diffviewer v0.1.2): desired output: something like: One potential option: `diffobj::diffStr()` already provides formatted HTML output and color highlighting for structural differences, with a JS backend that could be adapted into `diffviewer`. I've implemented a proof-of-concept in a fork: https://github.com/d-morrison/diffviewer/pull/4. Glad to PR if of interest? (I'm guessing we should reach out to the diffobj maintainers first)

title: option to use `waldo::compare()` to compare arbitrary R objects?
description: Would it possibly be in-scope to add options to use a javascript wrapper around `waldo::compare()` to compare `expect_snapshot_value()` outputs and `.rds` files generated by `expect_snapshot_file()`, instead of using `create_text_diff()`? Currently (with diffviewer 0.1.2), when snapshotting arbitrary R objects with `expect_snapshot_file()`, the output of `testthat::snapshot_review()` is not always very human-readable. For example, if you first run the following snapshot test: ```r test_that("iris is consistent", { tempfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") iris[1:5, ] |> saveRDS(file = tempfile) expect_snapshot_file(tempfile, name = "iris") }) ``` and then change it to ```r test_that("iris is consistent", { tempfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") iris[2:5, ] |> saveRDS(file = tempfile) expect_snapshot_file(tempfile, name = "iris") }) ``` and then run `testthat::snapshot_review()`, diffviewer displays: The output from `waldo::compare()` would be much more useful: --- Similarly for `expect_snapshot_value(style = "serialize")`: ```r test_that("results are consistent", { expect_snapshot_value(iris[1:5,], style = "serialize") }) ``` and then change the test to: ```r test_that("results are consistent", { expect_snapshot_value(iris[2:5,], style = "serialize") }) ``` The in-console waldo output is: In comparison, the diffviewer output launched by `testthat::snapshot_review("iris")` is: (not-human-readable) Even with `style = "deparse"`, the diffviewer output is not as readable as the in-console Waldo output, IMO: In some cases, I have the console output available for inspection; however, when pulling down snapshot changes from github (e.g., via `testthat::snapshot_download_gh()`), I may not have access to the console output. For example, recently I ran into an issue where the diffs were so extensive that they overflowed the Github CI logs, and the only way I knew of to inspect the changes was via `testthat::snapshot_download_gh()` and `testthat::snapshot_review()`. If this is at all in-scope, I'm glad to attempt a PR if helpful; I don't have much JS experience though, so I'd have to vibe-code most of it.

title: `visual_diff()` stalls for large diffs
description:
Ported from <https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/issues/1990>.

Really, if anyone's using such large snapshots it's arguable that they're the problem. That said, it would be nice if the shiny app used by snapshot_review() could make some concession for very large diffs, even if that just meant failing gracefully. Ideally some kind of pagination might be an alternative solution.

Here's a reprex. For me it takes around 1,000,000 lines before things become truly unusable.

``` r
text_a <- sample(c(stringr::words), 1000000, replace = TRUE) |> paste(collapse = "\n")
text_b <- gsub("ab", "cd", text_a)

path_a <- tempfile("text_a", fileext = ".txt")
path_b <- tempfile("text_b", fileext = ".txt")

writeLines(text_a, path_a)
writeLines(text_b, path_b)

diffviewer::visual_diff(path_a, path_b)
```

I'll hopefully be able to open a PR at some point to fix this, but no promises 😄

title: Could the widget be tweaked so that copying text is a bit easier?

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Should allow viewing files without diffs
description: This is something I've wanted for a while: to be able to just view a directory of files, without diffs. That would be useful for when the initial snapshots are created.

description: Maybe make automatically pick the ratio to find the largest size that still fits in the window?

title: Also compare dataframes?
description:
It would be nice if diffviewer allowed to also compare dataframes.

For my own use, I created the small helper function below that creates tempfiles from the dataframes to be able to use diffviewer:

```
compare_DFs <- function(DF_new, DF_old) {
    
  OLD = tempfile(pattern = "OLD_", fileext = ".csv")
  NEW = tempfile(pattern = "NEW_", fileext = ".csv")
  
  readr::write_csv(DF_old, OLD)
  readr::write_csv(DF_new, NEW)
  
diffviewer::visual_diff(OLD, NEW)

}

```

title: diffviewer fails to show differences in some PNG files
description:
With these two files, there are a few pixels that are different, but the visual diff does not color them in red.
However, `magick::image_compare()` does show the differences.

```R
oldfile <- "file1.png"
newfile <- "file2.png"

library(magick)
old <- magick::image_read(oldfile)
new <- magick::image_read(newfile)

# Shows difference
image_compare(old, new)

# Does not show difference
library(diffviewer)
diffviewer::visual_diff(oldfile, newfile)
```

![grided_default new](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86978/122116086-d08ee880-cdea-11eb-9e73-86526f511500.png)
![grided_default](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86978/122116090-d1277f00-cdea-11eb-8007-d6e3694e2b2a.png)


This is the difference image generated by `image_compare()`. I've added arrows pointing to the pixels that are different.

![diff](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86978/122117866-fd43ff80-cdec-11eb-9013-14d379749302.png)

Here's the info about the pixels that are different:

```R
old_data <- old[[1]]
new_data <- new[[1]]

idx <- old_data != new_data
which(idx, arr.ind = TRUE)
#>       dim1 dim2 dim3
```

title: SVGs generated by vdiffr are not displayed
description:
With svglite this works:

```r
file1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
file2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")

svglite::svglite(file1); plot(1:3); dev.off()
svglite::svglite(file2); plot(2:4); dev.off()

diffviewer::visual_diff(file1, file2)
```

But SVGs generated by vdiffr are not displayed:

```r
file3 <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
file4 <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")

vdiffr::write_svg(function() plot(1:3), file3, "plot1")
vdiffr::write_svg(function() plot(2:4), file4, "plot2")

diffviewer::visual_diff(file3, file4)
```

I don't know if the SVGs generated by @thomasp85's version of the vdiffr engine work with diffviewer. Do you have this branch online Thomas?

Even if the new engine works, it would be nice for vdiffr users to be able to compare the old SVGs to the new ones when they transition to vdiffr 1.0. Or we just assume the SVGs to be equivalent?
